result.bottom_line: Publish from TIGER/Line 2026, not from the state file, unless Montana State Library grants written permission. TIGER's use terms are explicit (not copyrighted, free to use, Census Bureau acknowledgement required). The state file (258,208 segments, exported 2026-09-30) has richer attributes and address ranges, but its metadata gives a disclaimer and no licence. Geometry agrees closely in both tiles (93.9 to 98.8 percent of each source's length lies within 15 m of the other), so the choice turns on legal clarity and cleaning, not on geometry.
result.recommendation: 1) Base layer: TIGER/Line 2026 county road files (roads layer, with FULLNAME, MTFCC and RTTYP) plus the TIGER 2026 ADDR address-range files for the address search (ADDR has no street names; names come from the EDGES file keyed by TLID, not tested here). All 56 Montana county road zips total 88,859,641 bytes (HEAD sizes). Credit the U.S. Census Bureau on the About page; carry the Census accuracy caveat (not for property transfers or engineering); avoid TIGER/Line or Census TIGER in product names (prudent inference from the trademark sentence, not a stated rule). 2) Clean before drawing or counting: merge or drop concurrent and doubled TIGER features (Benchland: 74.9 percent of in-tile length shares geometry with another TIGER feature; Billings: 18.8 percent); normalise names to one spelling (TIGER abbreviates, MSL spells out); treat blank names (11.0 percent in Billings, 27.0 percent in Benchland, 25.6 percent county-wide) and placeholder names such as 'Internal' as unnamed. 3) Only if MSL confirms in writing that derived tiles may be redistributed: enrich TIGER lines with MSL name parts, RoadClass, SurfaceType, Ownership and FromAddr/ToAddr ranges by a within-15 m match, and publish the match rate per tile. Until then, MSL is an internal comparison reference only, and even that use should be confirmed with MSL.
result.refuter_note: The recommendation stands. Legal basis: the TIGER terms (not copyrighted; free to use in a product or publication; acknowledge the U.S. Census Bureau as the source; no access constraint) are verified verbatim in the live roads, ADDR and EDGES metadata. The MSL metadata gives a disclaimer ('for no other purpose'), no licence grant, and MSL asserts its name as copyright text and credit in its live ArcGIS service, so MSL-derived tiles should not be published without written permission. Technical basis: on live MSL geometry the two sources agree in Billings (98.5 percent of MSL length within 15 m of TIGER; 94.6 percent the other way), so the choice is legal and cleaning-driven, not geometric. TIGER overlaps (13 to 22 percent in Billings; 66 to 75 percent in Benchland, depending on junction handling) are real and need cleaning; MSL overlap is 0.4 to 7 percent. The step the recommendation left untested now checks out: every ADDR TLID joins to Yellowstone EDGES, and 99.2 percent of matches carry a street name. The 401 North 27th sample gives the same picture in both sources: the nearest segments are 40 to 47 m away, and the MSL 400-block segment is about 260 m away, so an address point source is still needed to test the address match. The corrections change figures and wording, not the choice.

result.bottom_line: Microsoft US Building Footprints (ODbL) is the only statewide set measured here: 773,199 Montana polygons, all single-ring. In the Billings sample box, Overture repeats OSM geometry (428 of 441 outlines are identical to OSM), so it adds little independent shape there. Microsoft and OpenStreetMap are ODbL; Overture buildings are ODbL with CC BY 4.0 components. Any published per-tile footprint JSON from these sources carries ODbL share-alike duties. The USGS zoom 17 tile cache returned 404 in four requests, so the visual overlay used zoom-17-extent exports from the same service instead. Total download 41.2 MB; downloads folder deleted.
result.recommendation: Order of preference for publishing per-tile footprint data, ranked by legal basis (this is not a quality ranking; no accuracy was evaluated beyond the cross-source checks): (1) A federal public-domain footprint set, only after its authors and terms are verified. 17 U.S.C. 105 covers works prepared by federal employees; public-domain data carries no ODbL share-alike. Contractor-made data is not covered by that sentence and must be checked per dataset. FEMA and ORNL terms are the other worker's scope. (2) Microsoft US Building Footprints for Montana: ODbL 1.0, one licence, one bulk file of 773,199 polygons. Publish the tiles under ODbL with the licence copy or URI (4.2), the 4.3 notice on the map, and keep the whole tile set downloadable free in machine-readable form (4.6). Estimated size about 119 MB uncompressed at 5 decimal places before gzip. (3) OpenStreetMap buildings: ODbL with a credit line and same-licence duty; the Montana-wide extract was not measured, so coverage is unverified. (4) Overture buildings last: ODbL for the theme plus CC BY 4.0 components that need their own credit; in the Billings box most outlines repeat OSM, and its Microsoft-tagged features come from the Global ML Building Footprints release, not the US file. Do not mix public-domain and ODbL footprints in one tile file, because that likely puts the whole file under ODbL. The ODbL reading here is not legal advice; counsel should confirm the US position before publishing.

result.bottom_line: No alternative should replace nClimGrid-Daily. Two can supplement it under conditions: gridMET (4 km; author waiver of copyright; data through 2026-10-17; no-login OPeNDAP subsets) and Daymet (1 km; 1980 to 2025-12-31; no-login single-pixel API; license runs through the DOE-sponsored ORNL record and needs confirmation). PRISM is freely reproducible with attribution, but Oregon State University keeps ownership, so it does not meet the public-domain preference. The S3 by_station CSV named in the task is stale (last TMAX 2025-02-06), so the 2025 check used the current GHCN .dly. At Billings on 2025-06-15 the grids read from -3.0 to +1.2 F against the airport high of 82.9 F (gridMET tmin is 5.7 F low); every grid's July 2025 total was 0.56 to 0.84 in above the airport total of 0.95 in.
result.recommendation: Do not replace nClimGrid-Daily. Supplement, in this order: (1) gridMET, for 4 km daily tmax, tmin and precipitation up to the latest days, using OPeNDAP cell subsets (no login, no bulk download). Legal basis: the author statement "This work (METDATA, by John Abatzoglou) is free of known copyright restrictions." with the copyright waiver, plus attribution. Record the PRISM dependence and the midnight-MST day. (2) Daymet, as a 1 km per-location cross-check through 2025-12-31, only after the ORNL/DOE license is confirmed in writing and the single-pixel API terms are confirmed; no bulk netCDF pulls in CI (they need Earthdata Login). Legal basis so far: the Earthdata record "openly shared, without restriction", which the EOSDIS guidance says is subject to the sponsoring organization license. (3) Do not ship PRISM as a layer. It may be used internally as a check with attribution, but OSU retains ownership, which fails the public-domain preference in decision 7 unless counsel accepts the free-distribution grant. (4) NOAA normals and Climate at a Glance are context only (county or 30-year normals), not per-location history.

result.bottom_line: NOHRSC publishes one season-total snowfall GeoTIFF per water year, with files found for 2008-09 through 2026-27 to date. Measured files: 2,354,154 bytes (2025-26) and 2,402,986 bytes (2024-25), on a 0.04 degree WGS84 grid. At the Billings centre cell the two seasons read 33.85 and 50.29 (units not stated in the file; inches inferred). That is the option in this run that gives a per-water-year snow value for any location without a station, at 4 km resolution and as an analysis rather than a point measurement. SNOTEL has 97 Montana sites (96 active) at 4,250 to 9,200 ft, so it covers mountain points only. SNODAS gives daily 1 km snow depth and SWE, but five years of daily tars come to about 19.6 GB at the 2025 average. SNODAS solid precipitation (product 1025 IL01) could be summed by water year, but it needs the same daily downloads and is model output.
result.recommendation: 1) Snow by year at every location: NOHRSC season-total GeoTIFF per water year. Legal basis: NWS public-domain terms with three conditions (no ownership claim, no implied endorsement, no altered content presented as official). Store per-cell values for the Montana box (34,916 cells; 139,664 bytes raw float32 per season; about 2.46 MB JSON for five seasons, estimate). Five water years is about 12 MB of downloads (two measured, three assumed at the measured size). Units and accuracy must be confirmed before display. 2) Daily snow on the ground: SNODAS via NSIDC (G02158), only if the owner needs a daily history. Legal basis: NSIDC citation condition. Five-year backfill is about 19.6 GB at the 2025 mean (43.3 GB if the winter sample day is used as the per-day size). The 2021-2026 window is outside the 2014-10-09 to 2019-10-10 zero-error period; treat int16 32,767 values as errors. 3) Mountain point checks: SNOTEL (AWDB), about 76 KB of JSON per station per water year for six elements. USDA terms are unverified (usda.gov and nrcs.usda.gov policy pages returned 403 and 503). 4) CoCoRaHS: no bulk export found on the pages checked; do not scrape the ViewData pages. Data are CC BY (attribution). The NOHRSC analysis already assimilates CoCoRaHS observer reports (PDD), so a direct feed adds little for season totals.

SNODAS 32,767 cells on 2025-01-15 (25 depth, 9 SWE) lie between 46.20 and 48.78 N and 121.49 and 121.82 W, not a single cluster centred near 47.1 N, 121.8 W. Only one sample day was checked for this claim.

Legal basis for the NOHRSC option must also carry: the NWS trademark and visual-identifier limit; the rule that a site may not present its own information as official government information; the 17 U.S.C. 403 notice for copyrighted works made predominantly of NWS material; and the as-is and no-liability wording.
NRCS policies-and-links now returns 404 (record says 503). usda.gov policy pages still return 403. No USDA public-domain text found on the WCC page.
Units remain unknown. The TIFF ResolutionUnit tag reads INCH, but it describes 100 dpi print resolution, not data units. The PDD, snowfall page and index.js contain no units.
Minor: the user-guide sentence uses the greater-than-or-equal symbol in the PDF (the record writes >=). CoCoRaHS ListDailyPrecipReports is now 129,946 B.
open_questions: NOHRSC GeoTIFF units are not printed in the file or in the PDD text read. Inches are inferred from magnitude and the location of the maxima. Confirm with NOHRSC (contact in the PDD) or the interactive map legend before any display.
NOHRSC accuracy for points away from observers is not stated in the PDD text read. Treat the grid as an analysis until an accuracy statement is found.

NOHRSC season-file names with 00 UTC end times returned 404 and 12 UTC end times returned 200 in three tests, consistent with the PDD (season totals aggregate daily 12 UTC analyses). Intermediate regenerations within the 5-day window were not tested.
USDA public-domain statement not retrieved (usda.gov policy pages 403; nrcs.usda.gov 503). Needed before SNOTEL values are published.

SNOTEL update cadence and day boundary are not documented on the pages read. Only the observed two-day lag is recorded. dataTimeZone -8.0 is the station-list value; the local-time convention was not verified.
CoCoRaHS license discrepancy (CC BY 3.0 in the data statement, CC BY 4.0 in the footer of the same page) needs confirmation from CoCoRaHS before publishing CoCoRaHS-derived values.
CoCoRaHS water-year summary download link not located (the ViewData landing says it is available for download). Format and terms not checked.
GHCN-D US1 overlap with CoCoRaHS not checked here (covered by the GHCN-Daily worker).
The Montana box coordinates are approximate and not clipped to the state boundary, so box totals include neighbouring states.
Snow by year for a town or address needs a cell rule (which 0.04 degree cell serves a point). Not tested here.
SNODAS per-day sizes were measured for 2025 only; the 2021 to 2024 backfill uses 2025 as the proxy.
The five-year NOHRSC total (about 12 MB) assumes the three unmeasured seasons are close to the two measured (2.35 and 2.40 MB).

SNODAS solid precipitation (1025 IL01) summed by water year would give a model water-equivalent for every 1 km cell. Not built or tested here; it needs the full daily archive (about 19.6 GB for five years).
